symptom: Launcher processes and HTTP endpoints were alive, but the main backend settings and runtime fingerprint had silently changed to an isolated L1-04 bench workspace.

root_cause.summary: The backend CLI originally lacked an immutable startup workspace. The first fix rejected runtime Settings and Factory rebinds, but omitted a startup boundary: a stale settings object could still bind resident services to a bench workspace before HTTP guards existed. create_app now pins settings to KERNELONE_INSTANCE_WORKSPACE before any service owner is initialized.
root_cause.impact: A single backend became logically multi-workspace despite the one-backend/one-workspace invariant, making Launcher, ContextOS, receipts, and runtime projections appear hung or point at the wrong project.

verification.unit_tests: 72 original targeted tests plus 33 startup-binding regression tests passed
verification.live_recovery: Main backend restarted as PID 16333. Its first fingerprint and settings response both reported /home/dains/Documents/polaris with workspace_binding_match=true; a hostile cross-workspace Settings request returned 409 without drift.
verification.residual: The separate L1-04 backend still owns port 49978 but is independently overloaded/unresponsive; it was preserved and is not a main Launcher authority regression.

automatic_detection_rule: Treat workspace_binding_match=false on a registered instance as P0 and never describe that instance as healthy solely because /health or its ports respond. At create_app startup, correct settings to the process-bound workspace before resident services initialize.
